Appliances.$comment: Every listed appliance, including Microwave and Kettle, is given a default during FHS preprocessing. An input need not declare any of them. The accepted values exist only so a user can pin a default ('Default') or opt out ('Not Installed'). Otherdevices is deliberately absent: it is injected as a default like the others, but it represents an unavoidable background load that an assessment must not be able to pin or opt out of, so an input naming it is rejected. The pattern is anchored because patternProperties matches anywhere within a property name, so an unanchored alternation would also accept any name merely containing an appliance name (for example 'Ovenette'), which then reaches preprocessing as an unrecognised appliance. The 'not' constraint forbids only the case where Fridge and Fridge-Freezer are both explicitly 'Not Installed', so at least one cold appliance remains; omitting either or both keys is allowed because both are injected as installed defaults.

HeatSource.$comment: Charging sources are the core model's alternative to rated_charge_power with a charge control, and the two are mutually exclusive. The wrapper builds each source's control itself, on the same off-peak window used for direct electric charging, with state-of-charge setpoints: a PCM battery only charges once the source exceeds its phase change temperature, so expressing the hysteresis as a temperature would cap the heat source below the point it has to exceed.
HeatSource.description: Named sources that charge the battery, each either a direct electric element or a wet heat source such as a heat pump. Omit to charge by direct electric element at a rated power instead.

rated_charge_power.description: Rated charging power of the direct electric element (unit: kW).

then.$comment: The charging circuit's heat exchanger and flow characteristics are given separately from the battery's own, because charging and discharging may use different pipework and a different exchanger.

name.description: Name of the HeatSourceWet that charges the battery, such as a heat pump.

temp_flow_limit_upper.description: Maximum flow temperature the heat source may be asked for when charging, reflecting the charging circuit's limits (unit: °C). It should exceed the battery's phase change temperature, or the battery stores only sensible heat.

flow_rate_charging_l_per_min.description: Flow rate through the heat exchanger when charging hydronically (unit: litre/minute).

A.description: Slope of the charging heat exchanger's conductance correlation UA = A x ln(Re x flow rate) + B, which returns the exchanger's overall heat transfer coefficient in W/K, Re being the Reynolds number at 1 litre/minute (unit: W/K). Obtained by fitting the exchanger's measured performance. It may differ from the battery's own A where charging and discharging use different exchangers.

B.description: Intercept of the charging heat exchanger's conductance correlation UA = A x ln(Re x flow rate) + B, which returns the exchanger's overall heat transfer coefficient in W/K (unit: W/K). Obtained by fitting the exchanger's measured performance. It may differ from the battery's own B where charging and discharging use different exchangers.

velocity_in_HEX_tube_at_1_l_per_min_m_pe.description: Water velocity in the charging heat exchanger's tubes at a flow rate of 1 litre/minute, from which the velocity at the charging flow rate is scaled (unit: m/s).

inlet_diameter_mm.description: Internal diameter of the charging heat exchanger's inlet tube, used with the velocity to obtain the Reynolds number (unit: mm).

oneOf.$comment: rated_charge_power is not required unconditionally: the core model offers two mutually exclusive charging configurations, and it belongs only to the direct electric one. See the conditional below.

then.description:
Party wall element for all party wall types, with specific handling for cavity air movement heat loss.

For cavity party walls, this accounts for non-negligible heat loss due to air movement
within the cavity, as identified by research. The thermal resistance of the
unconditioned space (cavity) is derived from the party wall cavity type and lining type.
Five cavity types are supported:
solid, unfilled_unsealed, unfilled_sealed, filled_sealed, and defined_resistance.
Two lining types are supported:
wet_plaster, and dry_lined

u_value_whole_wall.$comment: Deliberately not cross-checked against party_wall_cavity_type. This is the transmittance of the whole element, covering both leaves, whereas thermal_resistance_construction describes the construction only as far as the wall's midpoint, so the whole-element value carries information the other inputs do not pin down and no cavity type implies a particular value for it. That includes solid and filled_sealed: those describe how the energy calculation treats the element, not the transmittance of the fabric. Tying this value to the cavity type would reject legitimate input. The limiting fabric standard is for the compliance report to enforce; this schema checks internal consistency and physical plausibility only, hence a sanity range and nothing more.
u_value_whole_wall.description: Whole-element (room-to-room) thermal transmittance of the party wall, in W/(m²·K), covering both leaves. Used only for the Building Regulations compliance report; it is not used in the HEM energy calculation, which derives party-wall heat loss from thermal_resistance_construction and party_wall_cavity_type. It is not derivable from those inputs, which describe the construction only to the wall's midpoint, so it is authored by the assessor from the full build-up. Only a sanity range is applied here; the limiting fabric standard is enforced by the compliance report.

allOf.$comment: 'required' guards the 'if' so it cannot match vacuously when party_wall_cavity_type is absent. Without it, 'properties' constrains nothing, every branch matches, and an element missing its cavity type is also told to supply a lining type - pointing the assessor at a field that may not apply once the cavity type is given.

power_limit_export.$comment: Upper sanity bound rather than a physical ceiling: the limit is expressed in kW, and entering the same figure in watts (3680 for a typical single-phase G98 connection) would otherwise validate and then never bind, leaving the run to proceed as though unlimited. 100 kW is far above any domestic connection - a 100 A single-phase supply carries roughly 23 kW, three-phase roughly 69 kW - so it rejects the unit slip without rejecting a real installation.
power_limit_export.description: Maximum AC power exportable to the grid, typically a Distribution Network Operator limit enforced by a G100-compliant export limitation device. Applies to the whole supply: generation surplus and battery discharge share the limit. Generation surplus above the limit is curtailed, and battery discharge is throttled so that unexported energy is retained as charge. Omit for no limit, leaving the inverter's AC capacity as the only ceiling (unit: kW).

ScheduleEntryForDouble.description:
A schedule entry that can be a direct value, repeating pattern, or reference.

Examples:
    # Direct float value (temperature setpoint)
    21.5

    # Repeating pattern (21.5°C for 8 hours, 18°C for 16 hours)
    {"repeat": 24, "value": 21.5}

    # Reference to another schedule
    "weekday_temp_schedule"

    # Complex repeating pattern with reference
    {"repeat": 7, "value": "daily_temp_pattern"}

    # Power level schedule
    2.5  # 2.5 kW constant power

oneOf.$comment: The exchanger area is required whenever at least one heat source is a HeatPump_HWOnly installed with a separately-supplied store, and forbidden whenever one is integral to its store. additionalProperties applies its subschema to every property, so 'at least one matches' is expressed by negating 'none matches'. Each 'if' also requires HeatSource: 'properties' constrains only the keys present, so without it a tank missing HeatSource entirely matches both branches, and is told both to supply the exchanger area and to remove it - the latter naming a property it will need once a heat source is given.

then.$comment: Absence is required by forbidding any value for the property, rather than by negating a required list, so that the reported error path names the offending property instead of echoing the whole tank object.
